newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-DURHAM INSPIRED BY BOON EXAMPLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DURHAM INSPIRED BY BOON EXAMPLE.

text.p: Durham stand on the threshold of their first English championship victory for 20 months unless Nottinghamshire can escape from trouble at Hartlepool on Saturday.

Under Australian captain David Boon, Durham have started the season with greater self-belief and require just eight Nottinghamshire wickets to provide concrete evidence of their new leader's influence.
Boon made 68 as Durham reached 331, a lead of 161, and Notts finished the day on 68 for two, still 93 behind. Durham's last win came against the same opponents in the last match of the 1995 season.

It was also a good day for English fast bowlers Darren Gough, who warmed up for the summer's battle against the Australian batsmen with a burst of five wickets for 11 runs against Glamorgan, and Devon Malcolm who took four wickets for Derbyshire against Surrey.

Gough comprehensively outbowled Pakistan's Waqar Younis at Headingley on a day when 18 wickets fell for 350 runs but, despite a purposeful 54 from Australian Darren Lehmann, Yorkshire still finished the day 163 runs behind.
Malcolm received some late punishment but took four for 95 as Surrey were bowled out for 267 despite 83 from England's Graham Thorpe. Derbyshire replied with 113 for two by the close.
A 14-year-old record set by Viv Richards and Ian Botham was almost broken at Northampton where Somerset staged a remarkable recovery.

Somerset looked in terminal decline at 73 for seven only to be revived by Graham Rose and Michael Burns, whose eighth-wicket stand of 170 in 41 overs was only two runs short of the county record set by the legendary test pair.
Rose hit 12 fours and one six in an unbeaten 109, his seventh first-class century, to help Somerset to a first innings lead of 105.
